sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Jackson County?
sections.html:
The Jackson County Tax Collector collects it, and the county's online tax portal lets you search a bill by tax year. The Property Appraiser values property, and the Board of County Commissioners and other taxing bodies set the rates.

The tax collector's own site has a due dates and discounts page that works as a calendar for the whole year, mixing property tax with vehicle and license deadlines. This guide pulls the property tax rows from it so a seller can see which date applies when a house goes under contract.

Jackson County sits in the Central Time zone, so deadlines that say "by midnight" follow local Central time, not Eastern. Mail-in discounts are tied to the postmark, so mail early in a month where the discount matters.

sections.h2: When are Jackson County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Collection begins in November, and the gross amount must be paid by March 31. The tax collector's calendar lists a discount for each month from November through February.

Property tax calendar rows from the Jackson County Tax Collector (jacksontc.com, Due Dates and Discounts)
MonthWhat the page says
NovemberCollection begins, 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchPay the gross amount by March 31
AprilUnpaid real property tax is delinquent April 1, with a 3% penalty

The same discounts apply to tangible personal property tax, which covers business equipment. A homeowner can ignore that line, but a landlord with furnished units or a seller who ran a business from the property should read it.

sections.h2: What happens when Jackson County property tax goes delinquent?
sections.html:
On April 1 a 3% penalty is added to the gross amount for real property. Within 45 days the delinquent list is advertised in a local newspaper, and the cost of that advertising is added to your bill.

In May the list of delinquent real estate taxes runs once a week for three consecutive weeks before the tax certificate sale. The tax collector sets the sale date in March, before the April 1 delinquency date, so a date can be known well ahead. A tax certificate is a lien the collector sells to an investor; after two years from April 1 of the issue year the holder can apply for a tax deed, and the clerk then holds an auction. The state opening bid for homestead property includes one-half of the latest assessed value in addition to the amounts due, which gives a homestead more protection than other parcels.

Tangible personal property works differently. Unpaid tangible tax picks up 1.5% interest per month on the gross amount, advertising within 45 days, and tax warrant processing starting May 1.

sections.h2: Is there an installment plan in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Yes. The tax collector's calendar describes a four-payment plan for next year's property tax, and applications are due by April 30. People already enrolled do not need to reapply.

  • First installment: due on or before June 1, with the program cancelled if the payment is not remitted by June 30.
  • Second installment: due before September 30.
  • Third installment: due by December 31.
  • Fourth installment: due by March 31.

The first-installment wording is worth a close read: the June row says "on or before June 1," while the cancellation rule says June 30. Call the tax collector to confirm which date applies to your account before relying on the later one. If you sell during the plan year, tell the closing agent which installments are paid so the tax is prorated correctly.

sections.h2: What homestead and assessment limits apply in Jackson County?
sections.html:
A Jackson County owner who makes the house a permanent residence by January 1 and files Form DR-501 by March 1 can claim up to $50,000 of homestead exemption. The first $25,000 applies to every tax, and the second $25,000 reaches only non-school taxes on assessed value over $50,000.

The Save Our Homes cap holds yearly assessed-value growth to the lower of 3 percent or inflation, with the 2026 cap listed at 2.7 percent. Non-homestead property is limited to 10 percent a year. Both limits end with a change of ownership, so a buyer often sees a larger bill than the seller did.

  • Seniors 65 or older may qualify for an additional local exemption if the county or city has adopted the ordinance and household income is within the limit.
  • A veteran with a 10 percent or greater service-connected disability may receive a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.
  • Homestead is lost when the home is rented or stops being the permanent residence.

Ask the Jackson County Property Appraiser which local ordinances apply to your address.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Jackson County valuation?
sections.html:
File a petition with the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, the TRIM notice, which the Property Appraiser mails in August. An exemption denial gets 30 days from the denial letter.

Start with the Property Appraiser for an informal review, since many errors in square footage or exemption status can be corrected without a hearing. Bring a deed, survey or contractor records if the property record is wrong. The appeal does not pause the bill entirely: the state calendar says petitioners must still pay the taxes they do not dispute before delinquency.

The calendar of local hearings, fees and deadlines is on the notice itself, so keep it with your closing file.

sections.h2: Will the November 2026 property tax amendment change my Jackson County bill?
sections.html:
Jackson County's government announced a town hall on October 13, 2026 about Amendment 3, a proposed property tax amendment on the November 2026 ballot, to discuss how it could affect local government funding and public services. The county's notice describes the amendment as proposed and presents no figures.

The ballot result, and any new law that follows, will decide what changes. Check the Florida Department of Revenue and the county's budget pages for the effective year before you build a number into a sale price. Until the property appraiser and tax collector post new rules, plan around the dates and rates on your bill.

sections.h2: What should a Jackson County seller do about tax at closing?
sections.html:
Request a written payoff from the tax collector, confirm what year it covers, and ask the title company to prorate the current year. Florida's deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and every party to the deed is liable for it.

  • Search the account by tax year in the tax collector's portal to see whether earlier years are open.
  • Ask about delinquent amounts and advertising costs if the account passed April 1.
  • Check for recorded liens at the Clerk before setting a closing date.
  • Tell the closing agent about installment payments already made.

A cash buyer can close around a delinquency or certificate sale date, with the title company paying the tax from your proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Jackson County property tax?
faqs.a: March 31 is the last day to pay the gross amount. Discounts of 4%, 3%, 2% and 1% apply for November through February.

faqs.q: What penalty applies after April 1 in Jackson County?
faqs.a: A 3% penalty is added to unpaid real property tax on April 1. Tangible personal property instead carries 1.5% interest per month.

faqs.q: When is the Jackson County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The tax collector sets the date in March, before the April 1 delinquency date. Check the collector's announcements for the current year.

faqs.q: Can I pay Jackson County taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. Apply by April 30 for next year's plan, then pay in June, September, December and March. Confirm the June due date with the office.

faqs.q: Does a sale of my Jackson County house reset my property tax?
faqs.a: For the buyer, yes. A change of ownership ends the Save Our Homes cap and the 10 percent non-homestead limit, and the property is reassessed at just value the following January 1.
